extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, appellate counsel, IP practitioners, and legal academics interested in Federal Circuit outcomes
extracted.subtask_description: An empirical/statistical review of all Federal Circuit patent decisions in a calendar year (2024), reporting counts, rates, timing, and judge-level statistics. Focuses on appeals and writs involving patent-law issues from PTAB, district courts, ITC, and Court of Federal Claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology and Scope — inclusion/exclusion and counting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: This year's study covers all patent cases decided by the Federal Circuit in 2024, whether by precedential opinion, nonprecedential opinion or summary affirmance. It includes merits decisions and rulings on writ petitions, but it excludes denials of leave to appeal, dismissals for lack of finality, stipulated dismissals and remands, and dismissals for mootness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes appeals and writ petitions from district courts, the PTAB, the ITC and the Court of Federal Claims only when the Federal Circuit decided at least one patent law issue. If the court resolves companion cases separately, the decisions are counted separately. If the court decides multiple appeals in a single opinion, all are counted as one decision. Cross appeals count only when the Federal Circuit decides them. When the Federal Circuit grants rehearing and vacates an opinion, the study disregards the retracted opinion and counts only the replacement decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caseload and Case Origins
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of patent decisions and breakdown by origin (PTAB, district courts, ITC, Court of Federal Claims) and by PTAB subcategories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example counts: 288 patent cases in 2024; PTAB cases (153, 53%); district court appeals (124, 43%); ITC (6) and Court of Federal Claims (4). PTAB docket subtypes include IPRs, original-prosecution cases, ex parte reexaminations, covered-business-method cases, non-CBM post-grant review cases, inter partes reexaminations, and interferences; report counts and percentages for each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmance Rate (definition and computation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Circuit fully upheld the lower court or agency — affirmed or dismissed on all issues or denied all relief in mandamus cases — X% of the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report overall affirmance rate and by origin (e.g., PTAB affirmance rate, district court affirmance rate). Provide context: overall 81% in 2024; PTAB 86%; district court 73%. Also report share of mixed results and full reversals/vacaturs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party Success Rates (patent owners/applicants vs challengers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rates at which patent owners/applicants and patent challengers fully prevailed, fully lost, or achieved mixed results across appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide overall and origin-specific splits (e.g., patent owners/applicants fully prevailed 19% overall, 27% in district court appeals, 13% in PTAB appeals). For appellants specifically, report their win/loss rates (e.g., patentees as appellants prevailed outright 9% and lost nearly 79%). Also report challengers' appellant success (e.g., challengers as appellants prevailed 22% in 2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opinion Type Distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize decisions as precedential opinions, nonprecedential opinions, or summary dispositions and report their shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report percentages and note differences by case origin (e.g., summary affirmance rate ~45% in IPR appeals vs ~15% in district court appeals). Define summary dispositions: mostly single-line decision orders under Federal Circuit Rule 36, but also treat other decisions of one page or less as summary dispositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Disposition Definition and Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat most summary dispositions as single-line Rule 36 orders; also treat other decisions of one page or less as summary dispositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Federal Circuit Internal Operating Procedure 10.6, a panel may not issue a Rule 36 affirmance unless all three judges agree. When reporting summary-disposition rates, clarify whether non-Rule-36 one-page dispositions are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition Speed — docketing to decision (median months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Median time from docketing to date of decision for true patent appeals (excluding writ petitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report year-to-year medians (example: 19.5 months in 2024; 16.8 in 2023; 13.8 in 2022). Distinguish between true appeals and writ petitions when computing medians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lag from ready date to oral argument/submission (median months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Median lag time from the ready date — typically submission of a compliant joint appendix — to oral argument or submission on the papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report medians and trends (example: 9.3 months in 2024 vs 6.4 in 2023). Note operational factors affecting lag (e.g., calendar additions, courtroom renovations) and typical wait times for oral argument (10–11 months recently).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-argument decision time (median months) by opinion type
rubrics_metrics.description: Median time from argument/submission to issuance of decision for precedential panel opinions and for nonprecedential opinions (excluding summary affirmances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report separate medians (example: precedential 3.2 months in 2024; nonprecedential 1.6 months). Provide prior-year comparisons to show trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge-level Productivity (decisions authored and case counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of patent cases decided per judge and counts of opinions authored (precedential vs nonprecedential).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report totals per judge (examples: Judge Prost 98 decisions decided; Judge Lourie 82; Judge Lourie authored 23 opinions (5 precedential, 18 nonprecedential)). Also identify quickest writers by median post-argument times (e.g., Judge Taranto medians).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship and Opinion Authorship Statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Number and type of opinions authored by each judge in patent cases (precedential vs nonprecedential).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate authorship counts from mere appearances on panels. Note exclusions (e.g., writ petitions included; unsigned per-curiam decisions not included in authoring statistics).

rubrics_metrics.name: En Banc Decisions and Rehearing Activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Count and description of en banc decisions and rehearing en banc grants; report scheduled oral arguments for rehearing en banc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report when the court heard or granted rehearing en banc (example: LKQ Corp. v. GM decided en banc in 2024; EcoFactor rehearing en banc granted on damages issue). Note how rare en banc patent decisions have been historically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel Dissent Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate and count of panel dissents in patent cases during the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report total dissents and percent of cases (example: 10 dissents in 288 cases, <3.5%). Identify frequent dissenters and context (e.g., Judge Newman historically most prolific but suspended in 2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandamus Petitions and Grant Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of mandamus petitions decided and the number granted by the Federal Circuit in the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report absolute counts and highlight notable patterns (example: 18 mandamus petitions with only one grant in 2024, incl. Western District of Texas petitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 101 (Patent Eligibility) Cases and Outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of patent eligibility cases decided and patentee success rate in overturning ineligibility rulings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report that all Section 101 cases were appeals by patentees in 2024 (40 cases) and the number of successful reversals (2 of 40). Note special circumstances (one reversal on party-presentation grounds rather than merits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent-Friendliness Index (PFI) — definition, computation, caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: PFI = 100 + (% decisions entirely favoring patent owner/applicant) - (% decisions entirely against patent owner/applicant). The calculation disregards mixed decisions and dissents from denials of rehearing en banc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report PFI for court and for each judge. Provide caveats: rough measure due to random distribution of cases among judges, exclusion of mixed outcomes, equal weighting of all cases irrespective of significance, and sensitivity to small-sample effects. Example: Federal Circuit PFI 50.7 in 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Affirmance Rate by Case Origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of appeals resolved by summary disposition (summary affirmance) broken out by origin (e.g., IPR vs district court).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report that summary affirmance rate in IPR appeals was ~45% and ~15% in district court appeals. Contextualize with complexity of issues: district court appeals tend to be more complex and less routine, hence fewer summary affirmances.

rubrics_metrics.name: District-level Outcomes and Performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and affirmance/reversal records for appeals originating from particular district courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report per-district totals and outcomes (examples: District of Delaware 22 decisions, 19 affirmances (86%); Eastern District of Texas 12 decisions, 11 affirmances (92%); Western District of Texas cases dropped from 26 to 14 with 2 affirmances and 4 reversals in regular appeals). Note whether mandamus petitions are concentrated in a district and their success.
